approach: The internal energy of a diatomic ideal gas is five halves of nRT, since it has five degrees of freedom at ordinary temperatures.

steps.text: Write the internal energy formula for a diatomic gas.
steps.why_this_step: A diatomic molecule has three translational and two rotational degrees of freedom at room temperature, giving five in total.

steps.text: Substitute the given values and evaluate.

common_mistakes.text: Using the monatomic formula with three degrees of freedom instead of five, which gives 14.96 kJ instead of 24.93 kJ.
Leaving out the number of degrees of freedom and using U = ½nRT, which gives 4.98 kJ instead of 24.93 kJ.
